scope: Independent, source-linked verification of the published CS2 dashboard on 2026-10-26 (live capture at 00:51-00:54Z from a network-capable runner), the nine open Hotspawn fixtures the 23:03:48Z publication does not list, and the identity/clock conflicts that decide which external line may price them.
method: Every live fact below was fetched by .github/workflows/b3e91409-probe.yml and archived under data/research/b3e91409/live/ with its URL, UTC observation time, HTTP status, byte count and SHA-256 (manifest.json, sources.json). The published rows were re-derived offline from the inputs each row itself publishes by scripts/b3e91409_verify.py; the formulas are re-implemented there, not imported from the production ladder. No probability, pick, price or alias was written by this session: the live dossier only records observed prices and the printed rating formula. Hotspawn community '% picked' and HLTV fan votes were never read as inputs. Re-run at 01:22Z against the 2026-10-26T01:04:30Z publication (19 rows): 18 of 19 probabilities re-derive exactly, one fitted form model is not reproducible from its own published inputs, and all 19 published picks agree with this session's independently derived side.

items.area: Coverage: nine open fixtures are absent from the published list

The same public Hotspawn fixture array read at 2026-10-26T00:51:22Z returns 81 CS2 records and 19 open fixtures, and the rendered lobby at the same instant shows the same 19 cards. items.handling: The 00:43Z four-hour refresh (run 40250748384) completed at 01:15Z and published the 2026-10-26T01:04:30Z build: 19 open fixtures, 19 with a pick, 0 unresolved, 3 alias joins (origination.json counts). This session re-ran scripts/b3e91409_verify.py against that publication: 19 rows checked, 0 coverage gaps, 18 exact replays, 1 reproducibility error (B3-R08) and 3 notes (B3-R06). The live dossier captured at 2026-10-26T01:01:19Z contains the same 19 ids, and all 19 published picks agree on the side with this session's independent line (6 Polymarket books, 3 Thunderpick lines, 10 printed-rank models). items.area: Provider clock conflict on 1079202 FOKUS vs ex-Zero Tenacity
items.finding: Polymarket event 1252125 (cs2-fokus-zerote-2026-10-26) stamps its full-series market 6186062 and both map markets with gameStartTime '2026-10-26 18:00:00+00'. Hotspawn schedules the fixture at 12:00Z, Thunderpick row 2888795 starts at 12:00Z, and HLTV match 2399117 starts at 12:00Z. The six-hour disagreement is far outside the 60-second identity window, so the Polymarket book cannot be joined; the fixture is priced from Thunderpick 1.35 / 2.90 instead (68.2% / 31.8% after proportional margin removal).
items.handling: No rule was relaxed. The published 60-second identity rule correctly refuses the Polymarket event; the conflict is recorded here so the owner of scripts/originate.py can decide whether Polymarket's start-time field is a known platform offset for this competition. The dossier's Thunderpick quote carries its own URL and observation time.

items.area: Three verified rows publish no limitation text beside a wide or modelled number
items.finding: Re-checked against the 2026-10-26T01:04:30Z build (2026-10-26T01:26Z): the limitation text IS published, on the row itself (`matches[].limitations`) rather than inside the nested `origination` object, and `/unresolved/` renders it under "Why there is no line" / "Why not the featured line". The original note was therefore a checker defect, not a disclosure gap: the checker read only the nested object. Rows 1082792 (HOTU vs The Huns), 1093218 (Nuclear TigeRES vs UNiTY) and 1081159 (LFO 10 vs ex-6666) carry no limitations array in their origination object. For 1082792 that hides that 87.0% / 13.0% is a single-venue midpoint from a 0.10-wide book (bid 0.82-0.92 / 0.08-0.18); for 1093218 it hides that 58.3% is a median of two books; for 1081159 it hides that 39.0% is a fitted model with an 18.4%-64.5% interval. Every other published row carries its limitation text. The arithmetic in all three replays exactly, so this is a disclosure gap, not a data error.
items.handling: Fixed in this session's checker: `scripts/b3e91409_verify.py` now reads `analysis['limitations']`, then the row-level `limitations` list, and only notes a missing disclosure when neither carries text; `tests/test_b3e91409_verification.py::LimitationTests` pins both directions. The published rows were never edited.

items.area: One published probability is not reproducible from the row's own inputs
items.finding: Row 1081159 (LFO 10 vs ex-6666) publishes method model, provider "Own results-based model (bo3.gg series results)", probabilities 0.39044606 / 0.60955394, inputs with fitted points 825 and 923, rating_sd 114.7, n_series 10 and interval [0.1842, 0.645]. The predictive formula that turns those posterior means into a win probability is not published, and neither standard reconstruction matches the row: Valve's fit.js logistic (RD 75) gives 0.366143 / 0.633857 and a plain 400-point Elo gives 0.362592 / 0.637408, a 2.4-2.8 point gap. The likely explanation is that the fit integrates over the posterior spread, which pulls the estimate toward 0.5, but a reader cannot confirm that from the row. The pick is unchanged under all three computations (ex-6666).
items.handling: Reported, not edited: the row belongs to the publisher's ladder. scripts/b3e91409_verify.py now classifies a fitted results model as not replayable and prints the standard Elo on the same points so the size of the gap is visible; tests/test_b3e91409_verification.py pins the branch. Request for the owner of scripts/originate.py: publish the predictive formula (or the fitted coefficients) beside the posterior means so this row can be replayed like the other 18.

items.area: The two official rating inputs disagree by up to 34 points on the same fixture
items.finding: Four fixtures are priced by a research model rather than a market. On the same fixture, the two official rating sources the ladder can use imply very different probabilities under one printed Elo formula: 1079201 INOX Division vs Nemesis gives 12.3% / 87.7% from Valve points 1105 / 1455, but 46.8% / 53.2% from HLTV ranking points 10 / 32; 1081163 BakS vs Saint Sinners gives 78.8% from Valve 1044 / 810 but 50.4% from HLTV points; 1082793 5star vs 1WIN gives 17.8% from Valve 1110 / 1383 but 34.9% from HLTV points. The published rows name Valve as the input, so they are not misattributed; the flag is that a model pick is highly sensitive to which official rating is chosen, and HLTV's integer points compress low-tier teams toward 50/50.
items.handling: Published as a limitation with the exact points behind each figure. No number is overridden: the published Valve model stands, and this session's HLTV-based figure exists only in its own dated dossier (data/research/b3e91409/live/analysis.json) so a reviewer can see the spread. Request for the model owner: consider publishing both inputs, or state on the methodology page which official rating is preferred and why.
